dataset: OONI measurement aggregation API – daily per-country counts of anomalous, confirmed, failed and OK measurements
description: Daily country-level shares of OONI Probe measurements flagged as anomalous (or matched to a known block page) for websites, instant-messaging apps and circumvention tools. Measurements are run by volunteers; an anomaly is a deviation from a control measurement, not proof of censorship.

coverage.geographic: Countries where volunteers ran OONI Probe on the day in question (roughly 140 countries per day for web tests, far fewer with meaningful volume for app tests). Country-days with fewer than 50 measurements are not shown.
coverage.temporal: The 7 most recent complete UTC days, one value per country and day; older days persist locally until retention expires.

updateCadence.upstream: Measurements are published in near real time; daily aggregates keep changing for a day or two as late uploads arrive and are occasionally reprocessed

license.notes: The OONI data policy (https://ooni.org/about/data-policy/) refers to github.com/ooni/license/data, which states that the licence applies to all published OONI data, including data published on api.ooni.io. Sharing and adaptation are permitted for non-commercial purposes only, with attribution, and derived data must be shared under the same licence (share-alike). The percentages shown here are adaptations computed by this application from OONI's counts.

limitations: An OONI 'anomaly' is a measurement that deviates from a control measurement taken from a non-censored vantage point. OONI states that an anomalous measurement does not necessarily contain evidence of censorship and may be a false positive (transient network failures, CDN/geo differences, unreliable sites, test bugs). Anomaly shares must be read in aggregate and over time, never as a count of blocked sites.

'Confirmed' only means that a Web Connectivity measurement matched a block-page or DNS fingerprint known to OONI; fingerprints exist for a limited set of countries and networks, so a value of 0 % does not mean that nothing is blocked. In the aggregation API anomaly_count excludes measurements counted as confirmed or failed.

Coverage depends entirely on where, when and on which networks volunteers run OONI Probe and on which sites they test (global and country-specific test lists differ), so values are not comparable between countries like a survey statistic and can swing with the sample.

Country-days with fewer than 50 measurements for a layer are omitted as too small to be meaningful; this threshold is an application choice, not an OONI rule. For Web Connectivity each tested URL is one measurement, so 50 measurements can still come from a single probe run.

Messaging (WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, Facebook Messenger) and circumvention (Tor, Psiphon) layers pool the measurements of several tests; per-test shares are given in the record attributes. Tor and Psiphon tests show elevated anomaly rates in many uncensored networks.

The probe country is inferred by OONI from the probe's IP address (GeoIP); VPN use by volunteers can misattribute measurements. Territories absent from this application's country gazetteer (e.g. Gibraltar, Guadeloupe, Martinique) are not shown.
The most recent day can be incomplete while late measurements are still being uploaded; values are re-fetched every 6 hours and revised.
confidenceNotes: No per-value confidence is assigned. The source measures the share of volunteer-run OONI Probe measurements per country and UTC day that OONI's pipeline labelled 'anomaly' (deviates from the control; frequently a false positive) or 'confirmed' (matched a known block-page/DNS fingerprint). The percentages are derived by this application from OONI's published counts (anomaly_count or confirmed_count divided by measurement_count); the raw counts are kept in each record. These are measurement signals, not confirmed censorship events.

retention.note: One record per country, day and layer; kept for 30 days after the measurement day, then purged.

layers.name: Web anomalies (OONI)
layers.description: Share of OONI Web Connectivity measurements per country and day that were flagged as anomalous (possible, unconfirmed interference; often false positives).

layers.name: Web block-page matches (OONI)
layers.description: Share of OONI Web Connectivity measurements per country and day that matched a known block-page or DNS fingerprint (labelled 'confirmed' by OONI).

metric.name: Web measurements labelled confirmed by OONI

layers.name: Messaging-app anomalies (OONI)
